taxa.description: Major archaeal group including methanogens producing atmospheric methane and extreme halophiles living in salt saturations.
Extremophile archaeon isolated from a 2,600-meter-deep hydrothermal vent chimney ("white smoker") on the East Pacific Rise.
Extremely halophilic marine archaeon that synthesizes bacteriorhodopsin to harness light energy without chlorophyll.
Asgard archaeon closely related to the ancestral host lineage that engulfed the alphaproteobacterial ancestor of mitochondria.
Photosynthetic prokaryotes that triggered the Great Oxidation Event ~2.4 billion years ago, forever transforming Earth's atmosphere.
Colonial freshwater cyanobacterium producing gas vesicles to regulate buoyancy in the water column.
Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped coliform bacterium ubiquitous in vertebrate gut microbiomes and molecular genetics.
Filamentous soil bacterium known for complex morphological differentiation and production of clinical antibiotics and geosmin (scent of rain).
Soil-living amoeba that transitions from single-celled individuals to a multicellular slug and fruiting body in response to starvation via cAMP signaling.
Single-celled ciliate covered with thousands of coordinated cilia for locomotion and oral groove feeding.
Single-celled green alga with two anterior flagella, an eyespot for phototaxis, and a large cup-shaped chloroplast.
Dominant peat-forming bryophyte capable of storing up to 26 times its dry weight in water, vital for global carbon sequestration.
One of the earliest known land plants with fossilized vascular tissue, featuring simple dichotomous branching and terminal sporangia.
Sole surviving species of the ancient Ginkgoales order dating back over 270 million years, with distinctive fan-shaped leaves and motile sperm.
The world's most massive single tree species, native to the western Sierra Nevada mountains, with fire-resistant fibrous bark.
Small flowering plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae), the premier model organism for plant biology and genomics with first sequenced plant genome.
Primary staple cereal grain consumed by over half the human population, domesticated in the Yangtze river valley ~10,000 years ago.
Single-celled budding ascomycete yeast central to bread leavening, beer fermentation, and eukaryote cellular genetics.
Filamentous ascomycete mold that produces the beta-lactam antibiotic penicillin, revolutionizing 20th-century medicine.
Iconic mycorrhizal mushroom with bright red cap and white warts, forming symbiotic associations with birch and conifer trees.
Prized edible funnel-shaped forest mushroom with fragrant apricot scent and gill-like ridges.
Basal multicellular marine sponge lacking true tissues or symmetry, filtering water through a network of choanocytes.
Translucent cnidarian medusa with four horseshoe-shaped gonads, exhibiting radial symmetry and stinging nematocysts.
Extinct marine arthropod with three-lobed calcified exoskeleton and compound holochroal calcite-lens eyes.
Standard model organism for developmental genetics, neurobiology, and chromosome mechanics since Thomas Hunt Morgan (1910).
Highly intelligent coleoid cephalopod with complex decentralized nervous system, eight suction-armed limbs, and rapid chromatophore camouflage.
Apex marine predator possessing a cartilaginous skeleton, electroreceptive ampullae of Lorenzini, and serrated triangular teeth.
Tropical freshwater ray-finned fish noted for transparent embryos, regenerative capabilities, and extensive use in biomedical research.
Neotenic salamander that retains its aquatic larval form with external feathery gills into adulthood and can regenerate complete limbs and heart tissue.
Massive bipedal theropod dinosaur with crushing bite force exceeding 35,000 Newtons, stereoscopic depth perception, and acute olfactory lobes.
Transitional fossil between non-avian feathered dinosaurs and modern avians, possessing flight feathers, toothed jaws, clawed wing digits, and a bony tail.
Flightless Columbiform bird endemic to Mauritius, driven to extinction in the 17th century following human discovery and introduced invasive mammals.
North American sea eagle with iconic white head plumage, yellow hooked beak, and telescopic visual acuity.
World's largest living lizard species, native to Indonesian islands, hunting with anticoagulant venom glands and armored osteoderm scales.
Semi-aquatic egg-laying monotreme endemic to eastern Australia, featuring a duck-like electrosensory bill, beaver-like tail, and venomous ankle spurs.
Extinct machairodontine saber-toothed felid that roamed North America, armed with 28 cm maxillary canine sabers to subdue Pleistocene megafauna.
Large apex felid of the genus Panthera, noted for social pride hierarchy, sexually dimorphic mane in males, and resounding territorial roar.
taxa.habitat: Sub-Saharan African savannas and Gir Forest, India

taxa.description: Largest wild member of the Canidae family, famous for cooperative pack hunting, acoustic vocal howling, and ancestor of domestic dogs.
The largest known animal ever to have existed on Earth, reaching lengths of 30 meters and masses over 190 metric tons, feeding on krill via baleen plates.
Small rodent that is the most widely utilized mammalian model organism in biomedical research and genetic knockouts.
Great ape native to African forests and savannas, sharing ~98.8% DNA sequence identity with humans, demonstrating tool crafting and culture.
Archaic human species adapted to cold Eurasian climates, skilled in Mousterian stone tools, intentional burial rituals, and interbred with Homo sapiens.
Extant bipedal primate characterized by high cognitive adaptability, symbolic language, complex cultural institutions, technology, and global presence.

divergences.name: Last Universal Common Ancestor (LUCA)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: First self-replicating cellular entity with DNA, RNA, ribosomes, and ATP synthase.

divergences.name: Archaea - Asgardarchaeota / Proto-Eukaryote Split
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Emergence of Asgard archaea with proto-cytoskeletal elements and membrane remodeling capabilities.

divergences.name: Eukaryogenesis (LECA)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Endosymbiosis of alphaproteobacterium giving rise to mitochondria and nucleus.

divergences.name: Bacterial Crown Divergence
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Divergence of Cyanobacteria (photosynthesis), Proteobacteria, and Firmicutes.

divergences.name: Archaeplastida Primary Endosymbiosis
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Primary endosymbiosis of a cyanobacterium creating the first photosynthetic plastids/chloroplasts.

divergences.name: Embryophyta Land Plant Colonization
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Cuticle, stomata, and alternation of generations enabling survival on terrestrial land.

divergences.name: Tracheophyta (Vascular Plants)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Lignified xylem and phloem enabling upright vertical growth and transport of water/nutrients.

divergences.name: Spermatophyta (Seed Plants)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Evolution of seeds and pollen grains, freeing plant reproduction from standing water.

divergences.name: Angiospermae (Flowering Plants)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Flowers, double fertilization, and fruit encasing seeds for animal/wind dispersal.

divergences.name: Opisthokonta Divergence
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Posterior single flagellum and synthesis of chitin in cell walls / exoskeletons.

divergences.name: Crown Fungi (Eumycota)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Hyphal absorptive heterotrophy and specialized fungal spore dispersal mechanisms.

divergences.name: Dikarya Subkingdom Split
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Dikaryotic stage (n+n) in life cycle and complex fruiting body (mushroom) evolution.

divergences.name: Metazoan Crown Radiation
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Multicellularity, extracellular matrix (collagen), cell-cell adhesion, and nerve/muscle precursor genes.

divergences.name: Eumetazoa (True Tissues)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: True germ layers (diploblasty/triploblasty), gut cavity, and synaptic nervous systems.

divergences.name: Bilateria (Cambrian Explosion Clade)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Bilateral symmetry, triploblastic development (endoderm, mesoderm, ectoderm), and cephalization.

divergences.name: Protostomia Radiation
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Blastopore becomes mouth; divergence into molting animals (Arthropoda) and lophotrochozoans (Mollusca).

divergences.name: Deuterostomia Radiation
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Blastopore becomes anus, radial cleavage, and enterocoelous coelom formation.

divergences.name: Chordata Origin & Cranium Evolution
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, and post-anal tail.

divergences.name: Gnathostomata (Jawed Vertebrates)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Hinged jaws modified from gill arches and paired pelvic/pectoral fins.

divergences.name: Tetrapoda Land Transition
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Four-limbed locomotion, digits, lungs, and neck mobility enabling terrestrial invasion.

divergences.name: Amniota Divergence
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Amniotic egg with waterproof membranes (amnion, chorion, allantois) for dry-land incubation.

divergences.name: Archosauria & Dinosauria Radiation
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Erect gait, bipedal agility, proto-feathers, and efficient unidirectional air-sac respiration.

divergences.name: Mammalia Crown Radiation
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Mammary glands, three middle ear ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes), fur/hair, and endothermy.

divergences.name: Boreoeutheria & Euarchontoglires Split
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Placental reproduction giving birth to developed young and rapid post-K-Pg radiation.

divergences.name: Carnivora Split (Feliformia vs Caniformia)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Specialized carnassial shear teeth (P4/M1) for hyper-carnivorous diet.

divergences.name: Hominidae (Great Apes)
divergences.evolutionary_milestone: Bipedal adaptation, enlarged neocortex, tool use, and complex vocal communication.
